styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old harbour, Markthal and the rebuilt centre.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Boompjes, Depot and bold modern architecture.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Zoo, harbour boat trips and Kinderdijk windmills.

stays.why: Walk to Markthal, the old harbour and Centraal station. Best base for a first visit.
Modern waterfront by the Erasmus Bridge; quick metro to the centre and good river views.
Old harbour bars and cafés on the doorstep; central and lively in the evening.
Quiet and green next to the zoo and Centraal; good for families and longer stays.

food: Try a Dutch lunch: broodje haring (herring roll), kibbeling (fried fish) or a cheese sandwich.
Markthal: many stalls under one roof. Good for a cheap, quick meal; prices vary, check on the day.
Eat Indonesian rice tables (rijsttafel) or Surinamese roti; both are strong local food traditions.
Bars and cafés cluster around Oude Haven and Witte de Withstraat. Book dinner on weekends.
Supermarkets and takeaway shops keep everyday food costs down; a sit-down dinner costs more.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for Kinderdijk windmills: WaterBus ferry from the centre, check times and fares on the day.
Take the WaterBus to Dordrecht for a half-day of old streets and harbour views.
Rainy day? Spend it indoors at the Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen or the Maritime Museum.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the centre, the art and a harbour trip; add a night for Kinderdijk or Dordrecht.

month_notes: Jan: cold and wet, highs near 7°C. Pack a rain jacket and warm layers.
Feb: still cold, around 8°C, with fewer rain days than January.
Mar: cool at 11°C and often wet; bring waterproof shoes.
Apr: milder at 14°C, good for walking and cycling.
May: pleasant at 18°C; a good month for the harbour and parks.
Jun: warm at 21°C with about 11 rain days; long daylight.
Jul: warmest month, highs near 22°C, but expect rain showers.
Aug: warm at 23°C; busy summer season, book hotels early.
Sep: still mild at 20°C and a little drier; a good shoulder month.
Oct: cooler at 15°C and wetter; carry an umbrella.
Nov: cold and wet, around 10°C; plan indoor sights.
Dec: cold at 8°C with many rain days; festive lights in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate maritime climate: mild summers, cool winters and rain in every month. Pack layers and a rain jacket year-round.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 11–15 rain days every month. Showers pass quickly; a light rain jacket beats an umbrella in wind.

items.title: Mild summers
items.text: July and August peak near 22–23°C. Rarely hot; evenings stay cool, so bring a layer.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: December to February highs sit around 7–8°C with lows near 2°C. Wind off the river feels colder.

items.title: Windy city
items.text: It is flat and open, so wind is common. A windproof jacket helps on bridges and boat trips.

items.title: Best months: May to September
items.text: Warmest and brightest. May, June and September are the sweet spots for walking and cycling.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket, comfortable shoes for cobbles, and sunglasses for bright summer days.

transit.best: Metro and trams for most trips; walk or bike in the flat centre.

modes.text: Lines A/B/C run east-west; D/E run north-south via Beurs and Centraal. Services every 10 minutes by day.
RET buses cover the city. Buy tickets in advance; no sales on board.
Uber and Bolt work here; taxis wait at Centraal and main squares.
Possible, but parking and narrow streets make it a poor choice for a city visit.
The centre is flat and compact. Walk between Markthal, Oude Haven and the river.
The city is flat and bike-friendly. Rent a bike for longer rides along the river.
WaterBus ferries reach Kinderdijk and Dordrecht. Check times and fares on the day.
Centraal station links the city to the rest of the Netherlands. Pay with OV-Pay or an OV-chipkaart (about €8.50).
